restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 (C = 2224); total work over all processors, including the characteristic search (charged as the exact itemised allowance of 3.40e7 = 2^25.0190 solver thread CPU-seconds at 2^23 units per CPU-second = 2^48.0190 units, anchored to 247,285 measured thread CPU-seconds), the starting-solution search (2^37.83 units) and the table build (2^36.5 units), all in preprocessing.

Two-block messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' of 128 bytes; complete SHA-256 with standard IV, steps 0..31 on all three padded blocks, feed-forward and all 256 digest bits; outputs verified by full recomputation and accompanied by a verified 128-byte 32-step collision certificate.

32-step truncation of the 35-step attack of Li, Liu, Wang, Shi (CRYPTO 2026, ePrint 2026/1080), using its Fig. 6 characteristic and starting solution as advice; truncation, table and Step-2/3 tests follow hash-smash #26/#33 (winglock), re-implemented and re-measured as in #235 (mitchuski), with the certified 32-step witness and deterministic slice replay from #227 (yudduy).

One run of T = 2^46.0 first-block trials partitioned into G = 2^40.0 strictly i.i.d. groups of L = 64 blocks sharing W0..W14 (W15 = r15 + j mod 2^32, 8 trials per 256-bit word via 8-lane SWAR at 244 ops/trial, verified bit-for-bit in replay.py) with a counted Step-2/3 work cap of 221.0 T word operations (Stage-17 early abort; cap-stop <= 0.00114 by unconditional Cauchy-Schwarz across the G i.i.d. groups). Total work A + B + C + D + E = 2^43.742 + 2^48.021 = 2^48.093 <= 2^48.10 units (2^48.416 <= 2^48.45 ungrouped).

Heuristic bound: relies on the declared heuristics q-32step-matching-rate, step3-46-conditions, within-group-trial-independence, route-search-allowance, cpu-second-pricing (score-critical) and valid-tuple-pairs, starting-solution-measured, search-peak-memory (supporting).

heuristics.statement: A uniform first block M0 compressed with C_32 from the IV yields at least 2^-17.3583 expected valid tuples (Step 2) against TAB2 of 1,396,774,912 tuples.
heuristics.scope: The exact TAB2 and Step-2 tests of proof Section 4 with C_32 first blocks.
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact-enumeration prediction 2^-17.3254; four measured runs, 2^34 part-trials, 25,936 valid tuples, pooled 2^-17.3373 with 99% lower bound 2^-17.3583; corroborated by the retained tuple slice replay in experiment:fixed-witness-derivation and the Lipmaa-Moriai Step-2 carry tests in experiment:r32-prob-Verify and experiment:r32-w20-s0w5-carry.
heuristics.limitations: Large-scale rate runs are participant C executions; treats CV1 words as uniform for the Step-2 tests.

heuristics.statement: For a valid tuple each of the 196,608 (W14,W15) candidates conforms through step 22 and W16..W31 with probability at least 2^-46, and Step 3 succeeds with r >= 2^-28.415 (1 - 2^-20).
heuristics.scope: Steps 16..22 and W16..W31 of the second block; candidates grouped by W14 (12 groups of 2^14), charged in the second moment.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured cumulative stage rates through step 21 over 2^32.25 candidates match the condition mapping; full 32-step conformance is demonstrated constructively by the certified 128-byte witness (certificates/manifest.json and experiment:fixed-witness-derivation) and the W22/W23 carry experiments (experiment:r32-w22-s1w20-s0w7-cancel, experiment:r32-w23-s0w8-cancel).
heuristics.limitations: Independence beyond the W14 grouping is not proved; the 13 W20/W22 carry conditions after step 21 are extrapolated from the condition count and corroborated by the single certified witness.

heuristics.statement: Within a group of L = 64 first blocks sharing W0..W14 with W15 = r15 + j mod 2^32 (j = 0..63), the pairwise joint Step-2/3 success probability for distinct j != j' satisfies Pr[S_{g,j} and S_{g,j'}] <= 2^10 s^2, so by Bonferroni Pr[Z_g >= 1] >= L s (1 - 2^-30.84) across each of the G = 2^40.0 strictly i.i.d. groups.
heuristics.scope: Pairwise collision success events within a single 64-block group only; cross-group amplification over the G = 2^40.0 groups is strictly i.i.d. and the W_cap = 221.0 T cap-stop bound uses unconditional Cauchy-Schwarz Var(Y_g) <= L^2 E[X^2] requiring zero within-group independence.
heuristics.extrapolation: After 17 steps of SHA-256 diffusion from W15 (steps 15..31) and 13 dependent message-expansion words (W17, W19, W21..W31), distinct offsets j != j' produce full-avalanche chaining values CV1; corroborated across 256 * C(64,2) = 516,096 within-group pairs in experiment:fixed-witness-derivation (502/16,384 5-bit hits = 0.03064, 502/516,096 pairs = 0.000973 vs 0.000977 independent). Even a 1,024x pairwise correlation factor (2^10 s^2) loses only 2^-30.84 of the group success rate.
heuristics.limitations: The scaled experiment checks a 5-bit chaining-value predicate across 516,096 within-group pairs rather than the full 2^-45.819 Step-2/3 event.

heuristics.statement: The search that produced the published 35-step characteristic (S Sect. 3-4) costs at most 3.40e7 = 2^25.0190 solver thread CPU-seconds on the measurement machine (2^48.0190 units at 2^23 units per CPU-second).
heuristics.scope: Characteristic search only; charged once as preprocessing; its memory is declared under search-peak-memory.
heuristics.extrapolation: Itemised from measured data without downward rounding: 247,285 thread CPU-s (48,912 wall-s) for Steps 1-4 as run under /usr/bin/time -v (which already sums user+sys CPU time across all solver threads); Step-4 completion estimated at 0.2M-4.0M thread CPU-s (subtotal 4.25M = 2^22.0190 thread CPU-s); multiplied by x8 for S's selection loop (3.40e7 = 2^25.0190 thread CPU-s, > 137x the entire 57-call run) without double-counting the thread factor. Declared plausible, not established.
heuristics.limitations: S's own search time is unpublished and no run here reproduced Fig. 6; the Step-4 completion estimate and selection-loop factor of 8 are argued envelopes, not direct measurements.

heuristics.statement: One solver CPU-second on the measurement machine costs at most 2^23 target-compression units (2^34.12 primitive 256-bit word-RAM operations, 17.0 operations per retired instruction).
heuristics.scope: The STP+CryptoMiniSat runs of the characteristic and starting-solution searches.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured 2^30.03 instructions per CPU-second (callgrind count of a deterministic call against native CPU time) and opcode mix (multiply/divide/floating point 0.42%, unmapped 7.24%) leave 17.0 primitive 256-bit word-RAM operations per instruction at kappa = 2^23 (as in #134), with full sensitivity at 2^24 and 2^25 reported in Section 8.
heuristics.limitations: One single-thread calibration instance; instruction rate under the run's machine load.

heuristics.statement: E[C(V,2)] <= q * 2^-5 for the number V of valid tuples in one trial.
heuristics.scope: Valid tuples sharing one first block.
heuristics.extrapolation: 9 within-part pairs in 2^34 part-trials; cross-part term estimated from multiplicity sums with the observed correlation factor; charge exceeds the estimate by more than 20x.

heuristics.statement: Producing the starting solution costs at most 32 x 908.8 CPU-seconds (two measured SAT runs) at 2^23 units per CPU-second (2^37.83 units), above S's reported 2^34.3 in any unit up to one compression.
heuristics.scope: The advice values A4..A13, E8..E13, W12, W13.
heuristics.extrapolation: Two SAT runs of S's attack Step 1 task (solution through step 13, checked exactly), the second with S's printed single-bit conditions asserted; S's own solution is the advice.
heuristics.limitations: Comparability of our solution to S's is neither claimed nor needed; the anchor is the cost of the same task.

heuristics.statement: The route search (S's and ours) needs at most 2^33 bytes at its peak.
heuristics.scope: Memory of the characteristic and starting-solution searches, which run before the attack phase.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured peak resident set 5.25 GiB over all 57 search calls and both start runs; S's own search is assumed of the same model size.
heuristics.limitations: S's historical peak is not reported; the measured peaks are added to the memory bound anyway.
